previous_statement: Theorem 1.1 (Acorn trick — purification channel): The channel Phi^{d,r} acts as: (i) Apply double Schur transform Schur^{dr} to rho^{tensor n}. (ii) Measure the Young diagram register Y, obtaining lambda. (iii) Prepare |EPR_lambda> in the Specht register PP' and maximally mixed state I/dim(V_lambda^r) in the ancilla Weyl register Q'. (iv) Apply inverse Schur transform. Then Phi^{d,r}(rho^{tensor n}) = E_{|rho_bar>}[|rho_bar><rho_bar|^{tensor n}] by Lemma 3.3. Gate complexity: poly(n, log d, log 1/delta) via efficient Schur transform [BCH05, Har05].
new_statement: Theorem 1.1 (Acorn trick — purification channel): The channel Phi^{d,r} acts on n copies of rho (on C^d registers A_1,...,A_n) via the following 6 steps: (1) Apply Schur transform Schur^d to rho^{tensor n}, obtaining registers (Y, P, Q). (2) Perform weak Schur sampling: measure Y to obtain partition lambda with ell(lambda) <= d. (3) Introduce new registers Y', P', Q' and copy lambda into Y'. (4) Prepare the Specht EPR state |EPR_lambda> in registers (P, P'). (5) Prepare the maximally mixed state I/dim(V_lambda^r) in Q'. (6) Apply the inverse double Schur transform (Schur^d tensor Schur^r)^dag to registers (Y, P, Q, Y', P', Q'), mapping back to n copies of a bipartite state on C^d tensor C^r. Then Phi^{d,r}(rho^{tensor n}) = E_{|rho_bar>}[|rho_bar><rho_bar|^{tensor n}] by Lemma 3.3. Gate complexity: poly(n, log d, log 1/delta) via efficient Schur transform implementations [BCH05, Har05].
